biod: Add new fingerprint firmware updater Add new bio_fw_updater utility which replaces the private-overlay per-board fp_updater.sh from chromeos-firmware-fpmcu-BOARD packages. This new updater adds the following notable functionality to the update process: * Decodes RO and RW versions from packaged firmware files. This means that the RO version does not need to be hardcoded in a board specific shell script and the RW version does not depend on the firmware file name. This also means that the same updater can be shared among all boards and can live outside of the private-overlay. * Testability of the firmware updater components and logic. For a component that is critical to system security, testability should be top priority. The new updater has been written in a semi-abstract manor that allows for testing of the update logic. * Ability to add metrics reporting about the update process and firmware versions encountered in the wild. Note that this change does not currently enable metrics. Minimal unit-tests of the firmware file version decoder have been included, but more in-depth tests of all components will follow. BACKPORT: x86/kvmclock: set offset for kvm unstable clock VMs may show incorrect uptime and dmesg printk offsets on hypervisors with unstable clock. The problem is produced when VM is rebooted without exiting from qemu. The fix is to calculate clock offset not only for stable clock but for unstable clock as well, and use kvm_sched_clock_read() which substracts the offset for both clocks. This is safe, because pvclock_clocksource_read() does the right thing and makes sure that clock always goes forward, so once offset is calculated with unstable clock, we won't get new reads that are smaller than offset, and thus won't get negative results. Thank you Jon DeVree for helping to reproduce this issue. Fixes: 857baa87b642 ("sched/clock: Enable sched clock early") Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org Reported-by: Dominique Martinet <asmadeus@codewreck.org> Signed-off-by: Pavel Tatashin <pasha.tatashin@soleen.com> Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com> (cherry picked from commit b5179ec4187251a751832193693d6e474d3445ac) BUG=chromium:954636 TEST=manual - run vm with patched kernel to verify uptime looks right. factory_mode: refactor factory_enable_failed Refactor factory_enable_failed, so cr50 always resets if a reset is requested. This change also renames factory_enable_failed to be more specific. It renames ccd_hook_active to wait_for_factory_ccd_change so it's obvious what the variable is doing. It's waiting for the ccd_config change after we enable factory mode. Enabling factory mode can fail in a lot of ways, but by the time we called factory_enable_failed, the failure is specifically about saving the config. This change renames the function, so the failure is a bit more specific. If a reset is required, always reset the system even if saving the factory config failed. ccd_reset_factory_failed is triggered if the ccd changed hook isn't triggered quickly enough or if cr50 fails to save the ccd config. Cr50 has already wiped the TPM and has most likely saved some if not all of the factory mode state. Cr50 should still reset even if the config isn't saved to be safe. enable_ccd_factory_mode isn't used in the process to enable factory mode during init, so this change won't cause a cr50 reboot loop from cr50 trying and failing to enable factory mode during init. This only affects the RMA and factory mode enable vendor commands. BUG=b:129956462 BRANCH=cr50 TEST=Use rma and factory mode vendor commands to enable factory mode. crash: Add CL option to disable hold-off time. Add a --ignore_hold_off_time to crash_sender. This option will set the hold-off time to zero. In other words, crash_sender will assume that crashes are completely written out when it finds a .meta file with done=1, instead of making sure the .meta file is at least 30 seconds old so that other writes can complete. In the login-crash-loop scenario, we know that debugd will have completely written all the crash data out before launching crash_sender, so there's no reason to wait around.
